title: Rosalind and the Choir
premise: Rosalind Hartwell, a runaway apprentice hiding his magic in the city of Vellamere where spellcraft is punishable by death, is forced to accept a dying courier's map — a chart to the Hollow Choir, a buried vault holding the Emberstone that once ended the last mage war and could start another. Hunted by the Inquisitor General's spies and shadowed by a loyal friend who doesn't know what he carries, Rosalind must decide whether to destroy the stone, use it to restore magic openly, or surrender it to the crown. Betrayed by the mentor who taught him to hide, he instead claims the Choir's power as his own inheritance, shattering the outlawry in a public reckoning at winter's height. The book ends with magic legalized but bound by oath, Rosalind choosing truth over invisibility, and the long winter breaking.
about_author: R. M. Oyelaran is the pen name of a former choir singer turned archivist who writes fantasy about people caught between institutions and their own consciences. They live near a cold coast and collect maps of places that do not exist.

chapters.title: Charms for Copper
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Five years after fleeing his apprenticeship, Rosalind sells luck-knots and fever-charms in Vellamere's night market, careful never to work real magic. A routine sale goes wrong when an Inquisitorial clerk lingers too long. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of a life half-lived.

chapters.title: The Dying Courier
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A bloodied stranger collapses in Rosalind's rented room, pressing a wax-sealed map into his hands with a warning: 'The Choir must not sing for her.' The man dies before explaining who 'she' is. Emotional beat: terror disguised as reluctance; the trap of compassion.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Studying the map, Rosalind recognizes his old master's handwriting — the route leads through the fens toward the Hollow Choir, a place from childhood stories. He tries to burn it; the parchment won't catch. Emotional beat: dread curdling into fascination.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Vane
chapters.summary: POV Inquisitor Sera Vane. Vane, the crown's chief hunter of mages, learns a courier died carrying something and begins pulling threads through the city's registries. She is brilliant, patient, and genuinely believes magic killed her family. Emotional beat: sympathy for the antagonist's conviction.

chapters.title: Tamsin
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Tamsin Ferro, a lamplighter and Rosalind's closest friend, notices his fear and offers help without asking questions. Rosalind lies to her face for the first time. Emotional beat: loyalty strained by secrecy; warmth shot through with guilt.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Visit
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The curious clerk arrives at Rosalind's door with official questions about the dead man. Rosalind performs ignorance while concealing the map beneath loose floorboards. Emotional beat: the thrill and sickness of deception done well.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Fens
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rather than wait for arrest, Rosalind flees the city at dawn, following the map into the marsh country as the first true snows fall. He is followed. Emotional beat: grief for the small safe life already mourned as lost.

chapters.title: The Wayhouse at Mireholt
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. At a frozen wayhouse, Rosalind meets Brannoc, a gruff ex-soldier who claims to have known his master. Brannoc offers to guide him — but asks pointed questions about 'her.' Emotional beat: cautious alliance; trust extended on a knife's edge.

chapters.title: Vane's Net
chapters.summary: POV Vane. Vane identifies Rosalind as the courier's last contact and dispatches agents, requesting authority to use a captured mage as a tracker. Her methods grow harsher as the trail resists her. Emotional beat: power quietly corrupting a principled woman.

chapters.title: Tamsin Follows
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Unable to bear not knowing, Tamsin follows Rosalind's trail north, using city connections to stay ahead of Vane's agents. She finds evidence of the purge that drove hedge-witches underground. Emotional beat: loyalty transforming into moral awakening.

chapters.title: The Master's Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Brannoc reveals Rosalind's master Aldous helped seal the Choir twenty years ago — and that Aldous betrayed the other sealers to save himself. Rosalind realizes his whole exile was shaped by an old sin. Emotional beat: identity shaken; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Ambush on the Ice Road
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Vane's agents attack on a frozen causeway. Rosalind, cornered, uses real magic for the first time in five years to save Brannoc's life — a flare of power seen by witnesses. Emotional beat: exhilaration and horror; the hidden self finally surfacing.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Tamsin reaches Rosalind just as Vane's second wave closes in; she is captured in his place when he escapes. Rosalind must choose between the map and his friend. Emotional beat: guilt weaponized; love forcing courage.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Vane. Vane interrogates Tamsin gently, offering her freedom for information, and finds herself liking the girl she may have to break. Meanwhile Rosalind negotiates with fen-witch smugglers for passage to the Choir. Emotional beat: two mirrors — each protagonist compromising principle under pressure.

chapters.title: Descent to the Hollow Choir
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Guided by the map and Aldous's sealed warnings, Rosalind descends into the vault: a cathedral of standing stones where the Emberstone hangs silent, singing only to those with magic in their blood. Emotional beat: awe; the weight of inheritance.

chapters.title: Aldous Returns
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. His master appears at the vault mouth — alive, having faked his death, and revealed as the one who sent the courier. Aldous wants the stone to blackmail the crown into restoring mages' rights, by force if needed. Emotional beat: betrayal by the person who taught him everything.

chapters.title: The Song Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Alone with the Emberstone, Rosalind experiences its memory: the last war, the sealing, the ordinary people who paid for mages' ambitions. He understands why magic was outlawed — and why outlawing it failed. Emotional beat: clarity; the theme crystallized.

chapters.title: Winter's Height
chapters.summary: POV alternating Rosalind/Vane. Aldous seizes the stone and raises a storm over Vellamere; Vane, holding Tamsin, marches on the Choir with soldiers. All parties converge as the solstice blizzard breaks. Emotional beat: collision course; every secret now a weapon.

chapters.title: The Reckoning at the Stones
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. In the vault, Rosalind turns the Choir's own resonance against Aldous, unmaking his claim on the stone while refusing to kill him. Vane arrives to find the war she feared already answered differently than either side planned. Emotional beat: climax — power refused, truth spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: POV Vane. Facing Rosalind across the stones, Vane must choose between executing him per law or accepting his terms: magic restored under sworn covenant, its abuses answerable to a mixed council. Tamsin's testimony tips her. Emotional beat: an enemy becoming an architect of peace.

chapters.title: Breaking of the Long Winter
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The storm lifts; Rosalind returns to Vellamore publicly, testifies before the council, and takes his place as first Oathbound warden. Aldous, stripped of power, walks into exile rather than swear. Emotional beat: bittersweet victory; identity claimed at last.

chapters.title: First Light
chapters.summary: POV Tamsin. Weeks later, Tamsin watches Rosalind teach the first legal charm-class in a generation — nervous children, small honest magic. She forgives him fully, and he stops flinching at his own name. Emotional beat: resolution; the long winter ends in ordinary morning light.
